source.title: Attention with Markov: A Framework for Principled Analysis of Transformers via Markov Chains
source.authors: A. Makkuva; Marco Bondaschi; Adway Girish; Alliot Nagle; Martin Jaggi; Hyeji Kim; Michael Gastpar

page_placements.theme: Unigram/bigram (no-context) stages and plateaus before in-context mechanisms

record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses induction-head findings reported by other work, but its own experiments measure next-token prediction and the loss landscape on Markov data, not induction-head formation, the repeated-token copying mechanism, or loss by token index.
record.gate_note: The paper states that deeper transformers develop induction heads, but attributes that finding to prior work and does not measure heads itself. Its own loss and prediction results concern learning first-order Markov kernels; those do not establish the induction mechanism or the claim's defined in-context-learning measure. These related findings are recorded under fits_no_version. The paper also cites prior results on higher-order Markov learning through induction heads; those are not its own results.
record.test_reason: The paper's own experiments measure test loss and next-symbol predictions of transformers trained on first-order binary and five-state Markov chains. It identifies no heads, measures no copying behaviour and reports no loss by token index. Its statements that deeper models form induction heads are attributed to prior work (Rajaraman et al., Nichani et al., Edelman et al.). It therefore tests no claim version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors characterize the single-layer loss landscape on Markov data: global (bigram) minima always exist, and bad unigram local minima exist under weight tying when p+q>1. Untying turns these into saddle points, and deeper models empirically reach the global minimum. Induction-head claims are cited from prior work, not tested.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies Markov-kernel prediction and the loss landscape of transformers; it does not reproduce the original induction-head measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported Markov-prediction outcome varies with switching probabilities, weight tying, and model depth.

fits_no_version.finding: With weight tying and p=0.5, q=0.8, a 1-layer transformer converges to unigram loss H(π) and predicts the stationary π1. Without tying it reaches the entropy-rate (bigram) loss and predicts p.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In single-layer transformers on Markov data, weight tying with switching factor p+q>1 creates a bad unigram local minimum; untying removes it.

fits_no_version.finding: For p=0.2, q=0.3, 1-layer models with and without tying reach the global minimum and predict p (0.199 from averaged weights).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: With p+q<1, single-layer transformers learn the first-order Markov kernel regardless of weight tying.

fits_no_version.finding: 2-, 4- and 8-layer models first plateau at unigram loss, then drop to the bigram global minimum.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Depth of two or more lets transformers escape the unigram plateau on first-order Markov data. The authors attribute this, via prior work, to an induction-head mechanism but do not measure it.

record.peer_reviewed: ICLR 2025 (published under an alternative title, as stated in the text)
record.problems: The paper does not measure induction heads or loss by token index. Several reported loss and prediction values are shown in figures rather than tabulated; the text gives qualitative descriptions for some outcomes. Experiments are reported as averages across 5 runs in some settings, without error bars or confidence intervals.
record.rows_left_out: The full parameter sweep in Fig. 4 and the multi-state loss experiments in Fig. 5 are not listed row by row because they concern Markov-kernel learning, not a claim version's induction-head or defined in-context-learning measure. The text's cited higher-order induction-head findings are prior work, not study results.

untested.parts: No head identification, no previous-token-head composition analysis, no [A][B]…[A]→[B] copying measurement. Single-layer attention is shown to be negligible (ratio ≈0.01), but this concerns Markov-kernel learning.
No tracking of head formation or in-context-learning score over training. The plateau-then-drop in deep-model loss (Fig. 1, Sec. 4.4) is not linked to any measured head.
No large models and no measurement of loss versus token index.
No measurement of induction heads across families, sizes, runs or architectures.
Data switching probabilities and weight tying are varied, but only Markov-kernel versus unigram convergence is measured, not induction-head formation.
No few-shot task learning and no mechanism comparison.
No sub-step decomposition of head formation. The loss plateau at H(π) followed by a drop is not tied to head measurements.

record.verdict_notes: The record's classification and rows are accurate. Fig. 4 (p,q sweep) and Fig. 5 (five-state chain) are properly declared in rows_left_out. The paper notes an earlier version wrongly claimed deep models fail on higher-order chains, attributing this to insufficient training iterations; this concerns cited work, not induction-head measurement here.

versions.untested_parts: Does not identify heads, test composition with a previous-token head, or measure the [A][B] … [A] → [B] copying behavior.
Does not measure induction-head formation over training, loss by token index, or a coincident bump in the training loss. The reported loss curves concern convergence to Markov-model loss levels.
Does not test whether induction heads carry most in-context learning in large transformers or measure loss falling with token index in large models.
Does not measure induction behavior across model families, modalities, or training runs. Its depth and state-space experiments measure Markov prediction, not induction heads.
Varies Markov data properties and weight tying for Markov-kernel learning, but does not measure whether or when induction heads form or whether the claim's defined in-context learning persists.
Does not test few-shot task learning or compare its mechanism with induction heads.
Does not track induction-head formation as a sequence of sub-steps. A reported loss plateau followed by a further drop is not a measurement of head formation.

relation.reason: Induction-head mechanisms are discussed through prior work; the study's own results concern the loss landscape and Markov prediction.

tranche.reason: The study measures Markov-kernel prediction and loss trajectories, without testing induction-head formation, copying, or in-context loss improvement with token index.

source_check.notes: The unigram plateau and subsequent loss drop are supported, but do not establish an induction-head phase change. The supplied text is arXiv v2, dated 21 July 2025.
